column3: Poor (300 – 579): Individuals with scores in this range may find it challenging to qualify for credit or may be offered credit with higher interest rates. It indicates a higher risk of defaulting on loans.
Fair (580 – 669): While individuals in this range may be eligible for credit, they might still face higher interest rates. It suggests a moderate risk to lenders.
Good (670 – 739): This range is considered good, and individuals with scores in this category are likely to be offered better interest rates on loans. It indicates a lower risk to lenders.
Very Good (740 – 799): Scores in this range are considered very good, and individuals are typically offered favorable terms on credit products. They represent a low risk to lenders.

Excellent (800 – 850): An excellent credit score indicates a very low risk of default. Individuals with scores in this range are likely to qualify for the most favorable terms and interest rates on credit products.

Income is not required for a mortgage approval but is a factor in determining Debt-to-Income. Our readiness assessment for this criteria is based on general U.S. household income ranges. Most importantly income will be reviewed on the basis of stability and proof of income. Finally, income should be judged relative to a cost of living index and the associated affordability factors for the specific area of the loan applicant(s).
Very Good: $150,000 to $300,000 in annual income
Excellent: Greater than $300,000 in annual income

The LTV ratio is the loan amount relative to the appraised value of the property. A lower LTV is generally more favorable, as it indicates that the borrower has more equity in the property. For a readiness analysis it is ok to use the expected purchase price of the house.

NOTE: A general goal is to have 20% down payment for a loan but the government offers specific programs that permit lower down payments Conventional Mortgages: Lenders often prefer setting a maximum Loan-to-Value (LTV) ratio of 80% or lower. FHA Loans: The Federal Housing Administration (FHA) may allow for higher LTV ratios, FHA loans often have a maximum LTV of 96.5%, meaning borrowers can make a down payment as low as 3.5%. VA Loans: Veterans Affairs (VA) loans are available to eligible military veterans and typically do not require a down payment. As a result, the LTV ratio for VA loans can be 100% or higher. USDA Loans: The U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) offers loans with a focus on rural and suburban areas. These loans may also allow for higher LTV ratios. Private Mortgage Insurance (PMI): If a borrower makes a down payment of less than 20% on a conventional mortgage, they may have to pay for private mortgage insurance (PMI).

Front-End DTI (or Housing DTI): This includes the proposed monthly mortgage payment (principal, interest, taxes, and insurance) divided by the borrower’s gross monthly income. Ideally front-end DTI is 28% or lower.
Poor: Mortgage payment is greater than 28% of gross monthly income
Good: Mortgage payment is 20 - 28% of gross monthly income
Very Good: Mortgage payment is 10 - 20% of gross monthly income
Excellent: Mortgage payment is less than 10% of gross monthly income

Back-End DTI (or Total DTI): This includes all monthly debt obligations, not just the mortgage, divided by the borrower’s gross monthly income. It typically includes items like credit card payments, car loans, student loans, and other debts. Ideally back-end DTI is 36% or lower.
Poor: Mortgage payment and other monthly debt payments are greater than 36% of gross monthly income
Good: Mortgage payment and other monthly debt payments are 30 - 36% of gross monthly income
Very Good: Mortgage payment and other monthly debt payments are 20 - 30% of gross monthly income
Excellent: Mortgage payment and other monthly debt payments are less than 20% of gross monthly income

In addition to requesting the above information, the bank will ask you to complete a personal financial statement. A personal financial statement (PFS) is a summary of a person’s financial health. A PFS provides an overview of an individual’s financial position at a specific point in time and includes information about an individual’s assets, liabilities, and net worth. You should update and review your personal financial statement frequently!
Poor: You have NOT created a Worthsheet Personal Financial Statement
Excellent: You HAVE created a Worthsheet Personal Financial Statement
